title: Runtime is Bun 1.4
position: The project runs on Bun 1.4. This choice gives the TUI, a single binary build, and native TypeScript execution. The floor is Bun plus POSIX. Windows is a non-goal.
rationale: The team chose Bun 1.4 over a Node.js runtime. Bun runs TypeScript directly, so no build step runs before execution. It also builds one binary for distribution. Windows-first work was rejected because Bun plus POSIX is enough for the first releases.

title: Effect pinned to the v4 release candidate
position: Errors and JSON checks use Effect 4.0.0-rc, the release candidate line. Failures are Data.TaggedError values. Serialized output passes through Effect Schema before the CLI emits it.
rationale: The brief first fixed Effect at stable 3.22.1 because v4 was at release candidate stage. The owner then chose to move to the v4 release candidate at once and accept the API churn, so the codebase migrates before v4 goes stable. The team will bump to stable v4 when it ships.

title: Executable TypeScript only
position: Saved requests are executable TypeScript files only. The workspace has no .bru files, no YAML DSL, and no schema language.
rationale: The team rejected Postman-style collection formats. Plain TypeScript files need no special tool to read or run.

title: Unknown flags fail, ignored flags warn
position: An unknown flag stops the parse with a named error, while a recognized but unsupported flag prints a warning and the parse continues
rationale: Chosen so silent misparses cannot happen, while tolerating harmless flags from newer curl versions

title: License is MIT
rationale: MIT keeps the package easy to install and use. The brief records this choice with no rejected alternative.

title: Method is inferred when -X is absent
position: The parsed method is GET, and it becomes POST when the command carries a body
rationale: Chosen to match curl user expectations, where a data flag implies a POST without an explicit -X

title: Package name is @quality-sh/postui
position: The npm package name is @quality-sh/postui. The scoped package still installs its bin as postui.
rationale: The bare name postui is blocked by npm typosquat protection because the package post-ui exists. The team chose the scoped name. They did not try to remove the block or rename the command.

title: Curl input is word-split per POSIX quoting rules
position: The splitter resolves quotes, escapes, and line continuations per POSIX word splitting before flags are parsed
rationale: Chosen over ad-hoc whitespace splitting so any curl command a human pastes from documentation splits the way the shell would have split it

title: Publishing uses OIDC trusted publishing
position: npm releases publish through OIDC trusted publishing. The release.yml workflow runs on v* tags with id-token: write. An npm environment gate and org staged publishing give the final approval. No long-lived tokens exist anywhere in the release path.
rationale: The team chose OIDC trusted publishing over long-lived npm tokens. This choice keeps long-lived tokens out of the release path, so a leaked token cannot publish a package.

title: Serialized output passes the Effect Schema gate
position: The --json path validates its payload against the Effect Schema contract before the process emits it
rationale: Chosen so agents never receive shape drift; a schema break fails loudly instead of emitting malformed JSON

title: Test targets are vitest, bun:test, and node:test first
position: Test generation targets vitest, bun:test, and node:test first. The three share one shape, so each target needs only one small emitter. @playwright/test comes later because its request fixture is an outlier that needs real work.
rationale: The team chose one small emitter for each framework over a shared assertion DSL. Jest is a deliberate non-goal. Playwright as a library runs fine under Bun, so the team can add @playwright/test later.
